bib.title: GIT: A Generative Image-to-text Transformer for Vision and Language
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v5; legacy extraction listed TMLR 2022)

read.skipped: References skimmed; figure-only pages (qualitative examples) read as captions only.

question: Can one image encoder plus one text decoder trained with a single language-modelling loss, scaled in data and model size, unify image/video captioning, QA, classification and scene text recognition?
hypothesis: A simple architecture with scaling can reach SOTA without object detectors, tags or OCR.
contributions: GIT: one image encoder and one text decoder pre-trained on 0.8 billion image-text pairs with the language modeling task
New SOTA on many image/video captioning and QA benchmarks without detectors, tags or OCR; surpasses human on TextCaps
SOTA even on video tasks without video-dedicated encoders
Generation-based image classification (88.79% top-1 on ImageNet-1K)

method.summary: Contrastively pre-trained Florence/CoSwin image encoder feeds flattened features (linear+layernorm to D=768) concatenated with text embeddings into a 6-block randomly initialised transformer decoder with a seq2seq attention mask; trained on 0.8B pairs with LM loss, then fine-tuned per task. VQA, classification and scene text are cast as caption generation; video uses 6 frames with learnable temporal embeddings.
method.task: image-to-text generation (captioning, VQA, video, classification, scene text)

datasets.name: Pre-training mix: COCO, CC3M, SBU, Visual Genome, CC12M, ALT200M plus extra 0.6B crawled pairs
datasets.source: extra 0.6B collected following Hu et al. 2021a; not released
datasets.preprocessing: shorter side <=384, longer side <=640, re-saved JPEG quality 90 (39 TB), following Wang et al. 2021a

datasets.name: COCO, Flickr30K, nocaps, TextCaps, VizWiz-Captions, VQAv2, TextVQA, ST-VQA, OCR-VQA, VizWiz-VQA, MSVD, MSRVTT, YouCook2, VATEX, TVC, MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, TGIF-Frame, ImageNet-1K, MJSynth+SynthText, six scene-text test sets
datasets.split: Karpathy split for COCO/Flickr30K; server evaluation for test sets
datasets.preprocessing: duplicates of test/val images removed from intermediate VQA fine-tuning mix

models.name: GIT
models.architecture: image encoder + 6-block transformer decoder, self-attention over concatenated image and text tokens
models.init_from: image encoder: Florence/CoSwin contrastive; decoder random

models.name: GIT2
models.architecture: DaViT 4.8B encoder (UniCL pre-trained) + 0.3B decoder following BERT-Large

training.objective: language modeling cross-entropy on text tokens given image, label smoothing 0.1; for VQA loss only on answer and [EOS]
training.hardware: A100 on Azure Machine Learning; GPU count not stated

other.finetune_captioning: 10 epochs, batch 512, lr 2.5e-6; SCST same hyperparameters if used
other.finetune_VQA: 20 epochs lr 1e-5 (VizWiz-QA 40 epochs, 2e-5); input 384 for intermediate FT, 576 final
other.finetune_ImageNet: 10 epochs, lr 1e-5, batch 4096 full / 16 few-shot, no beam search
other.video_frames: 6 frames, equal interval, same random crop in training; uniform sampling center crop at inference

inference.decoding: beam search, beam size 4, length penalty 0.6 (default)
inference.samples: single run; no seeds or variance reported
inference.prompting: VQA: question is the text prefix and the answer is generated; classification: class name is the caption

other.imagenet_voc_prior: trie constrains tokens to the vocabulary

metrics.name: scene text accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match (MJ+ST) or caption contains the word (TextCaps FT)

eval.protocol: Karpathy splits and public servers; single run; no significance tests

results.claim: Model sizes and data: GIT 681M encoder, 0.7B total; GIT2 5.1B (4.8B DaViT encoder), 10.5B images, 12.9B pairs.
results.quote: As the performance exhibits no signs of plateau, we further scale up the model size to 5.1B and the number of pretraining images to 10.5B (12.9B image-text pairs).

limits: Authors: unclear how to control generated captions or do in-context learning without parameter updates.
Larger decoders did not help; result may not transfer to pretrained frozen decoders (authors, G.3).
Generative VQA/ImageNet is harder: about 1.2-1.5 points below discriminative Florence with the same encoder.
No seeds or variance; 0.6B of 0.8B pairs are non-public; GPU count and compute not stated.
Pre-training data not guaranteed free of toxic language.
